title: The 10 Best Hole Saw Kits
subtitle: Hole saw sets for wood, drywall and metal, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A hole saw kit cuts clean round holes for door locks, recessed lights, pipes and wiring. We ranked 10 best-selling kits from Diablo, Milwaukee, Lenox, Bosch, Amazon Basics and value brands on rating, review volume and features: bi-metal or carbide teeth that can cut metal, sizes up to 4 in or more, a quick-change arbor, and a case. Carbon steel kits are cheap and cover big sizes but only cut wood, drywall and plastic. Prices run from $21.69 for KATA's 25-piece kit to $169 for Milwaukee's 28-piece contractor kit.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

avoid.name: PETUOL Hole Saw Set, 22 Pcs Metal Hole Saw Kit with 3/4 in to 5 in (19mm-127mm)
avoid.flag: Sold as a metal kit, not rated for metal
avoid.verdict: The title calls it a "Metal Hole Saw Kit", but the listing's own bullets say the saws are carbon steel, not suitable for hard metal, and meant for softwood, plastic, drywall and thin PVC.
reasons: The title says "Metal Hole Saw Kit", while the material bullet says heat-treated carbon steel and "Not hard metal suitable". A buyer shopping for a metal-cutting set gets a wood and drywall set.
The application bullet lists softwood, plastic plate, plasterboard and thin PVC board only, with a cutting depth of about 25 mm.
For metal, the Amazon Basics 9-piece bi-metal set costs $5.46 more and is rated for mild steel and aluminum. For wood and drywall, the KATA 25-piece covers up to 6 in for $21.69.

buyers_guide.q: Bi-metal, carbide or carbon steel: which do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Carbon steel saws are the cheapest and come in the biggest sizes, but they only cut wood, drywall and plastic. Bi-metal saws have high-speed steel teeth welded to a flexible body, so they cut wood and mild steel and last longer. Carbide-tipped saws are for stainless steel and other hard metal. If you'll ever drill a steel box or a metal door, buy bi-metal at minimum.

buyers_guide.q: What size hole saw do I need for a door lock?
buyers_guide.a: Most US door knobs and deadbolts need a 2-1/8 in hole through the face of the door and a 1 in hole in the edge for the latch. Check the lock's template first. DEWALT and others also sell dedicated lock installation kits with a jig that clamps to the door.

buyers_guide.q: What is an arbor or mandrel?
buyers_guide.a: The arbor (also called a mandrel) is the shaft that holds the hole saw and the pilot bit and goes into your drill's chuck. Small saws usually use one arbor and larger saws another. Quick-change arbors such as Diablo's Snap-Lock Plus, Milwaukee's quick-release and Bosch's SpinLOCK let you swap saws without unscrewing them.

A saw can only cut as deep as its cup. A 2x4 stud is 1-1/2 in thick, so a deep-cut saw like the Diablo (2-3/8 in) goes through a stud in one pass. Many cheap carbon steel kits cut only about 1 in deep, so thicker stock takes two passes from both sides.

buyers_guide.q: How do I get the plug out of a hole saw?
buyers_guide.a: Saws with wide slots let you push the plug out with a screwdriver. Some arbors, like Diablo's, eject the plug without tools. Drilling a small hole near the edge of the plug before you finish the cut also makes it easier to pop out.
